itineraries.title: Teardrop of Joy - 5 Day Itinerary
editorial: Colombo is the obvious way in or out for international travellers, so our loop around the emerald isle began and ended in the capital. Over five days, we climbed the hilltop of Sigiriya, walked the hills of Ella, and eventually descended on the beaches of Mirissa.
What if we had more time?
We’d take the long route from Dambulla to Ella, with pitstops in Kandy for the Temple of the Tooth and Nuwara Eliya for the tea country.
The scenic Kandy to Ella train route, which wasn’t operational during our visit, is a favourite among western tourists!

days.title: Day 1 - Sigiriya
editorial: Our trip started with an early morning arrival in Colombo, with a pre-booked taxi waiting to take us from the airport to Sigiriya (about four hours away).
We stopped at Dambulla, the town neighbouring Sigiriya, and spent an hour admiring the intricate artwork at the Buddha cave temple.

We took a short nap at our hotel in Sigiriya, before setting off for the climb at 4:00PM. It’s too hot to hike while the sun is overhead. It took us an hour to reach the top, but you could easily spend longer stopping to soak in spectacular sights.
Sigiriya is a more accessible and austere Machu Picchu in many ways, with the Lankan citadel predating it’s Peruvian cousin by a millennium.
You could hire guides at both Dambulla and Sigiriya, but we chose introspection over information.

days.title: Day 2 - Ella
editorial: We left early the next day for Ella. Our five-hour drive made memorable by the serenity along the roads as well as on it. Sri Lankans navigate narrow lanes with a civility that their South Asian brethren can only dream of.
Ella is bougie in the best possible way. It almost feels like the gateway towns to US national parks, but with Sri Lankan characteristics.
Spend the evening walking along the train tracks to the picturesque Nine Arches Bridge (about 30 mins from town). If you wait a while, you’ll get to see a train pass along the tracks.
When you’re done clicking pictures, continue towards Little Adam’s Peak for sunset. There is a shorter route from town, which we discovered only after choosing the scenic-but-longer version.
At night, the clouds descended onto the hills, reminding us of the wonderful Monteverde cloud forest in Costa Rica.

days.title: Day 3 - Ella + Mirissa
editorial: We walked back to the Nine Arches, this time for photos from the tea estate at the base of the bridge. We intentionally skipped the tea estate tours as we’d done those back in India (in Munnar, Kerala), but we highly recommend doing one if it’s your first time in the area!
Even in mid-March, the hills were astonishingly lush. Sri Lanka has a rainforest-like vegetation that feels cosier than large parts of the India that are covered in grasslands.

After checking out, we drove down to Mirissa along an immaculate national highway. We reached Mirissa around sunset, which is exactly when a beach town should introduce itself. The pace drops, the light softens and suddenly doing nothing feels like an item on the checklist.

days.title: Day 4 - Mirissa
editorial: We slept in instead of going whale-watching or snorkelling. No regrets.

Most water activities leave early because the sea is calmer in the morning. You’ll need to reserve your place on the tour at least a night before. Nearby Weligama beach is also a popular spot for surfers (especially beginners).
We abandoned adventure for a lazy day under the Lankan sun. For the very reasonable price of 2,000 rupees (or $7), we got beach beds with coconut water and iced coffee included.
The evening is best spent walking along the beach and reflecting on how you can feel this relaxed every day for the rest of your life.

days.title: Day 5 - Colombo
editorial: We drove back to Colombo for our flight home later in the day.

One of us had spent time here as a child, so we walked around the Galle Face promenade to reminisce. Colombo was, is, and perhaps will always be, the most orderly city in South Asia. Nearby One Galle Face is a posh modern mall if you fancy shopping.
Our last stop was the Seema Malakaya temple, where Buddha statues overlook an algal lake. An oasis of calm in the middle of the city.
Sadly, we did not have time to see the distinct looking Jami Ul-Alfar mosque.
